lessons.title: Introduction to Terraform & IaC
lessons.content_md:
# Introduction to Terraform & IaC

Infrastructure as Code (IaC) means defining your cloud resources in code files that can be versioned, reviewed, tested, and automated — just like software.

## Why IaC?

| Manual (ClickOps) | Infrastructure as Code |
|-------------------|----------------------|
| Click through console | Write declarative config |
| Undocumented | Self-documenting |
| Unreproducible | Exact same every time |
| No audit trail | Git history |
| Error-prone at scale | Automated |

## IaC Tools Comparison

| Tool | Provider | Language | Approach |
|------|----------|---------|----------|
| **Terraform** | Multi-cloud | HCL | Declarative |
| CloudFormation | AWS only | YAML/JSON | Declarative |
| Pulumi | Multi-cloud | Python/TS/Go | Imperative |
| Ansible | Any | YAML | Procedural |
| CDK | AWS | Python/TS | Imperative |

## Terraform Basics

Terraform uses **HCL** (HashiCorp Configuration Language):

```hcl
# main.tf
provider "aws" {
  region = "us-east-1"
}

resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  ami           = "ami-0c55b159cbfafe1f0"
  instance_type = "t3.micro"

  tags = {
    Name        = "FlyBeta-Web"
    Environment = "production"
  }
}
```

## The Terraform Workflow

```bash
# 1. Initialize (download providers)
terraform init

# 2. Preview changes
terraform plan
# + aws_instance.web will be created
#   + ami: "ami-0c55b159cbfafe1f0"
#   + instance_type: "t3.micro"

# 3. Apply changes
terraform apply
# Do you want to perform these actions? yes
# aws_instance.web: Creating...
# aws_instance.web: Creation complete after 35s

# 4. Destroy when done
terraform destroy
```

## Declarative vs Imperative

```
Imperative (HOW):          Declarative (WHAT):
"Create a VPC"             "I want a VPC"
"Create a subnet"          "I want a subnet in that VPC"
"Create an instance"       "I want an instance in that subnet"
"Attach a volume"          "I want a volume on that instance"

Terraform figures out      You describe the end state.
the order automatically.   Terraform makes it happen.
```

## Key Concepts

| Concept | Description |
|---------|------------|
| Provider | Cloud platform plugin (AWS, GCP, Azure) |
| Resource | A single infrastructure object |
| Data source | Read existing infrastructure |
| Variable | Parameterize configs |
| Output | Export values |
| Module | Reusable group of resources |
| State | Terraform's record of what exists |

# Variables, Outputs & Modules

## Variables

Parameterize your infrastructure for reuse across environments:

```hcl
# variables.tf
variable "environment" {
  description = "Deployment environment"
  type        = string
  default     = "dev"

  validation {
    condition     = contains(["dev", "staging", "prod"], var.environment)
    error_message = "Environment must be dev, staging, or prod."
  }
}

variable "instance_type" {
  type    = string
  default = "t3.micro"
}

variable "db_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true  # won't show in logs
}
```

```hcl
# main.tf — using variables
resource "aws_instance" "app" {
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  tags = {
    Environment = var.environment
  }
}
```

### Setting Variables

```bash
# CLI flag
terraform apply -var="environment=prod"

# .tfvars file
# prod.tfvars
environment   = "prod"
instance_type = "t3.large"

terraform apply -var-file="prod.tfvars"

# Environment variable
export TF_VAR_db_password="supersecret"
```

## Outputs

Expose values after apply:

```hcl
# outputs.tf
output "instance_ip" {
  description = "Public IP of the web server"
  value       = aws_instance.app.public_ip
}

output "db_endpoint" {
  description = "Database connection string"
  value       = aws_db_instance.postgres.endpoint
  sensitive   = true
}
```

```bash
terraform output instance_ip
# 54.123.45.67
```

## Modules

Modules are reusable packages of Terraform resources:

```
project/
├── main.tf
├── variables.tf
├── outputs.tf
└── modules/
    └── web-server/
        ├── main.tf
        ├── variables.tf
        └── outputs.tf
```

```hcl
# modules/web-server/main.tf
resource "aws_instance" "this" {
  ami           = var.ami
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  tags          = { Name = var.name }
}

# modules/web-server/variables.tf
variable "ami" { type = string }
variable "instance_type" { type = string }
variable "name" { type = string }
```

```hcl
# main.tf — using the module
module "web_prod" {
  source        = "./modules/web-server"
  ami           = "ami-abc123"
  instance_type = "t3.large"
  name          = "prod-web"
}

module "web_staging" {
  source        = "./modules/web-server"
  ami           = "ami-abc123"
  instance_type = "t3.micro"
  name          = "staging-web"
}
```

## Terraform Registry Modules

```hcl
module "vpc" {
  source  = "terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws"
  version = "5.0.0"

  name = "flybeta-vpc"
  cidr = "10.0.0.0/16"

  azs             = ["us-east-1a", "us-east-1b"]
  public_subnets  = ["10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24"]
  private_subnets = ["10.0.10.0/24", "10.0.20.0/24"]
}
```
